$comment: Every build-tooling review names the exact advisory identifiers, dependency path, current caller/input boundary and expiry. Missing, malformed or additional identifiers fail the production gate. Patched runtime dependencies do not qualify for tooling exceptions. See docs/privacy-security.md.

reviewed.advisory: image-size ICNS/JXL/HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
reviewed.justification: Metro Assets.getAssetData/getAssetSize reads image bytes from developer-selected workspace files while bundling. Both affected format detectors are installed, and filenames/extensions are not a safety guard. The supported source/configuration belongs to the developer already executing the build; no supported lower-trust image upload writes these source assets. This code is build tooling, outside the player bundle. The review covers only the two named advisories and this current input boundary.
reviewed.fixNotes: Upstream2.0.3 patches both advisories. Vinext now selects that compatible2.x patch through a scoped override. Metro still requires1.2.1 through ^1.0.2 and calls its default function/path-capable API; globally overriding to2.x changes that contract. No compatible1.x patch is listed. Retain this named Metro review until its caller/dependency updates; do not downgrade Expo57.

reviewed.advisory: uuid missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6 when buf is provided
reviewed.justification: The installed xcode pbxProject.generateUuid calls uuid.v4() with no buffer while rewriting a developer project. GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq concerns v3/v5/v6 with an explicit output buffer; none of those functions is called by this observed path. This tooling does not ship in the player bundle. The review covers the named advisory and current caller only.
reviewed.fixNotes: Patched in uuid >= 11.1.1, but the fix lives inside a transitive dependency of Expo's own tooling. Forcing an override into xcode's internals risks breaking iOS project generation for an unreachable code path. Adopt it when Expo updates xcode upstream.

reviewed.advisory: GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm: stack exhaustion through deeply nested patterns
reviewed.path: @101/controller-native > expo > @expo/metro-file-map > micromatch > braces; source build/lint > fast-glob > micromatch > braces
reviewed.justification: The installed recursive parser is affected. In the supported callers, Metro constructs watcher patterns from fixed strings and executable developer configuration; fast-glob patterns come from developer source AST or lint configuration. Filenames are matching inputs, not patterns. These inputs already belong to the developer who executes the build/configuration, so the claimed lower-trust pattern-to-process boundary is absent. This review covers the named advisory and current caller paths only; accepting lower-trust patterns requires a fresh assessment.
reviewed.fixNotes: No upstream patched version is listed. Do not downgrade Expo 57 to the unrelated major version suggested by npm. Reassess upstream fixes and pattern provenance at review.

reviewed.advisory: GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv: extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements during RSA verification
reviewed.justification: The affected verifier is installed, but Expo uses it to verify signatures it just generated with the local private key, or to validate an operator-supplied self-signed certificate that must match the provided private key. The iOS keychain path parses certificates without verifying attacker signatures. Current app configuration has neither EAS nor update code-signing certificates; the SDK builder permits only selected @101 dependencies. No supported caller exposes the dependency's certificate-issuing server API or accepts an attacker-supplied RSA signature. This review is advisory-specific; new certificate/signature inputs require reassessment.
reviewed.fixNotes: No upstream patched version is listed. Preserve Expo 57; reassess upstream fixes and any lower-trust signature or certificate API at review.
